title: Lancashire Hotpot
subtitle: Slow-braised lamb under a crispy potato crust
excerpt: A northern British classic of slow-braised lamb shoulder under a tight-fitted layer of sliced potatoes that go crispy on top. It needs time in the oven but very little work.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from Lancashire hotpot tradition. The defining feature is the layered potato lid that acts as both lid and serving element.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be assembled a day ahead and kept in the fridge unbaked. Add 10 minutes to the initial covered cooking time.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 150C / Gas 3 for the braise, then 220C / Fan 200C / Gas 7 for the potato crust finish

content.text: Slice the potatoes thinly and evenly so they cook through at the same rate. A mandoline helps but a sharp knife works fine.
Heat the oven to 170C. Season the lamb generously. Heat a splash of oil in an oven-safe stockpot over high heat. Brown the lamb in batches until dark on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add the onion and carrot to the pot. Cook for 5 minutes until the onion softens.
Return the lamb. Add the stock, Worcestershire sauce, thyme, and bay leaves. Stir and bring to a simmer.
Lay the potato slices over the top in neat overlapping rows. Brush generously with melted butter. Season with salt.
Cover the pot tightly with a lid or foil. Bake at 170C for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Remove the lid. Turn the oven up to 220C. Bake uncovered for a further 20 to 25 minutes until the potato top is golden and crispy.

items.symptom: Potato top is pale and not crispy.
items.cause: Oven not hot enough for the uncovered stage.
items.fix: Increase to 220C and cook uncovered for 20 to 25 minutes.

items.symptom: Lamb is still tough after 90 minutes.
items.cause: Temperature was too low or pieces were too large.
items.fix: Cover and return to the oven for a further 20 minutes.

items.symptom: Sauce has evaporated and is dry.
items.cause: Pot seal was not tight enough.
items.fix: Add a splash of hot stock and cover tightly with foil.
